note: The closest thing in this batch to the ICP as stated on the Harry Edmonds call. He runs warehouse and operations for a wholesale distribution business supplying Target, Walmart, Amazon and the US grocery chains, and rose fast into it — 'I rose the ranks of my company so fast that I have so much responsibility now' — which reads as the 'or equivalent' in the criterion even though he is not the owner. Income is settled by behaviour rather than claim: he put $6,000 on one credit card inside ten minutes of hearing the number, with no price objection. Neglected health is nearly verbatim — 'I concentrated on work. I concentrated on my relationship and I kind of put my health last.' Good-to-great fits at 33 with a college-athlete base, clean nutrition, macro tracking and weekly yoga; he is chasing a six-pack back, not a rescue. And he is the opposite of the excluded profile: not close to 50 lb overweight, and someone who says 'I love the gym. I love the pump. I love the nutrition part.' The one thing the ICP does not measure and should is the clinical criterion — two MRI-confirmed bulging lumbar discs — which is the recorded observation that the stated ICP has no clinical screen, showing up again in a core-fit prospect who closed.
